title: Protein structures, opened to discovery
summary: Researchers can explore predicted protein structures through an openly accessible database, creating a starting point for biological questions.
reached: Researchers using the AlphaFold database and server. This record does not claim a patient outcome.
ai: Predicts molecular structures from learned patterns.
people: Researchers supply questions and test predictions experimentally.
took: Biological expertise, suitable sequences and experimental validation.
held: Database launched in 2021; provider timeline describes later releases. Individual downstream benefits need follow-up.
limits: A prediction is not a cure. Confidence varies, and use permissions depend on the service.
cost: Research time, compute and laboratory resources; access terms vary.
first: Explore one protein relevant to a research question and identify which prediction needs experimental checking.
review: Source located by AI; outcomes not independently verified

title: More time before the flood
summary: A Nature study reports reliable forecasts of extreme river floods in ungauged watersheds, with useful lead time before an event.
reached: The 2024 paper describes forecasts available in over 80 countries. It does not establish how many lives were saved.
ai: Learns hydrological patterns to forecast river flow.
people: Researchers evaluate forecasts; local responders decide how warnings become action.
took: Hydrological data, forecast access and a local warning-and-response network.
held: Deployment reported in the 2024 study; local warning uptake requires separate follow-up.
limits: Forecast skill differs by basin. A warning only helps if people receive it and can respond.
cost: Connectivity and local response capacity; public forecast access described as free.
first: Find the forecast coverage for one watershed and ask who would receive and act on its warnings.
review: Source located by AI; local outcomes not independently verified

title: Everyday details, described aloud
summary: Be My AI offers image descriptions within Be My Eyes, with human assistance available when a person needs more help.
reached: Blind and low-vision users. The provider describes the service; independent benefit measurement is not established here.
ai: Describes images and responds to follow-up questions.
people: Users interpret descriptions and can seek assistance from human volunteers.
took: A supported phone, an internet connection and useful image capture.
held: Announced in 2023; the current provider page describes the feature.
limits: Descriptions can be wrong. This record does not establish suitability for safety-critical decisions.
cost: App access is described as free; phone and connectivity are needed.
first: Try describing a non-sensitive everyday object and compare the description with a trusted human account.
review: Source located by AI; participant outcomes not independently verified

title: Language research, led by its speakers
summary: Masakhane connects participatory research and open resources for African-language NLP, with community involvement central to the work.
availability: Open research; coverage differs by language
reached: African-language researchers and contributors. Availability for a particular language needs checking.
ai: Models support translation and related language tasks.
people: Speakers contribute data and evaluate what a model gets right or wrong.
took: Speaker participation, permissioned language data and task-specific evaluation.
held: The source describes ongoing work. Benefits to a particular community need local testimony.
limits: An available model does not establish reliable translation in every dialect or setting.
cost: Contribution time, coordination and appropriate compute resources.
first: Choose a language and review existing resources with a speaker before planning a translation experiment.
review: Source located by AI; language-specific outcomes not independently verified

title: Spoken stories become searchable text
summary: Whisper supplies open-source speech-recognition models for transcription, giving builders a tool for working with spoken material.
reached: Builders and researchers. This record describes capability rather than a measured community benefit.
people: Record with permission, check transcripts and decide what should be preserved.
took: Permissioned audio, a suitable computer and a speaker who can review errors.
held: Public repository available at review; downstream results require follow-up.
limits: Performance varies by language and audio quality. Transcripts may invent or omit content.
cost: Local compute and review time; hosted services can have separate charges.
first: Transcribe a short, consented recording and compare each line with the speaker’s intended meaning.
review: Documentation located by AI; downstream outcomes not independently verified

title: A useful assist for newer workers
summary: Research on customer-support workers reports productivity improvements from AI assistance, with different effects across experience levels.
reached: Workers in the studied setting. Improvements varied; results cannot be assumed for another workplace.
people: Workers judge suggestions and resolve customer issues.
took: A defined workflow, relevant knowledge and evaluation across workers.
held: The cited paper reports the studied period; it does not establish lasting benefit elsewhere.
limits: Productivity is one outcome. Worker autonomy and workload need separate assessment.
cost: Tool access, integration and supervision; not priced in this record.
first: Compare one low-stakes task with and without assistance, recording both time and quality.
review: Research source located by AI; external transfer not verified

title: A teaching idea gets a starting point
summary: Khanmigo offers AI tools for lesson preparation and tutoring. Access differs between teachers, families and school implementations.
reached: Eligible educators and learners. This listing does not establish learning gains.
ai: Drafts teaching materials and guides practice.
people: Educators check content and remain responsible for teaching decisions.
took: Eligible access, subject expertise and a way to assess learning without the tool.
held: Provider describes current offerings; learning effects need separate evidence.
limits: Teacher access does not automatically provide student access. AI can make mistakes.
cost: Teacher and learner plans have different terms; check the provider.
first: Draft one activity, verify it yourself, then assess whether it helps someone explain the idea independently.
review: Source located by AI; learning outcomes not independently verified

title: A forest can tell you what is happening
summary: Rainforest Connection uses acoustic monitoring and AI to identify sounds associated with threats and wildlife activity.
availability: Projects and tools; local arrangements apply
reached: Conservation partners and monitored ecosystems. Benefits depend on local response.
ai: Classifies environmental audio to surface signals for review.
people: Partners install devices, interpret alerts and choose how to respond.
took: Permissioned sensors, power, connectivity and trusted local stewardship.
held: Provider describes operating projects; sustained protection needs site-level evidence.
limits: An alert is not proof of wrongdoing. Monitoring needs local agreement and review.
cost: Hardware, maintenance and local response capacity.
first: Ask a local steward which sound could answer a useful question before choosing recording equipment.
review: Source located by AI; site-level outcomes not independently verified

title: A new route through stubborn plastic
summary: Researchers used machine learning to help engineer FAST-PETase, an enzyme shown to break down tested PET plastics in laboratory conditions.
availability: Research result; commercial access not established
reached: Research teams. Scaled environmental cleanup is not demonstrated by this source.
ai: Proposes enzyme mutations for experimental testing.
people: Scientists test performance and design the chemical process.
took: Laboratory expertise, suitable PET material and controlled reaction conditions.
held: Reported in 2022; this listing does not establish subsequent industrial performance.
limits: The result concerns PET under studied conditions, not all plastics in an open environment.
first: Map one PET waste stream and identify a research partner before considering an enzyme trial.
review: Source located by AI; industrial outcomes not independently verified

title: What happens at sea becomes visible
summary: Global Fishing Watch combines satellite information and machine learning to make patterns of activity at sea easier to inspect.
reached: Researchers and ocean-governance communities. This record does not infer enforcement outcomes.
ai: Finds patterns in vessel information and satellite observations.
people: Analysts examine evidence; communities and authorities decide what follows.
took: Data access, interpretation skills and knowledge of local maritime contexts.
held: Platform available at review; individual governance gains require follow-up.
limits: Patterns can be incomplete. A vessel signal alone does not establish illegal conduct.
cost: Analysis time and connectivity; check data terms for reuse.
first: Explore one coastal area and list what the map can establish and what requires local evidence.
review: Source located by AI; enforcement outcomes not independently verified
